title: Canonical truncation interchange characterized by its pentagon
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with a t-structure [def-weil-t-structure], not necessarily bounded. Write $L_b=\tau^{\le b}$, $R_a=\tau^{\ge a}$ and let $\iota^b_K:L_bK\to K$ and $\pi^a_K:K\to R_aK$ be the canonical truncation maps [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. For integers $a\le b$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_{a,b}:R_aL_b\xrightarrow{\sim}L_bR_a.$$
For every $K$, its component is the unique morphism $v:R_aL_bK\to L_bR_aK$ satisfying the pentagon equation
$$\iota^b_{R_aK}\circ v\circ\pi^a_{L_bK}=\pi^a_K\circ\iota^b_K.$$
The isomorphism and this uniqueness assertion are in $\mathcal T$ itself.
